display_title: [XLA:GPU] Allow Triton scans over non-last dimensions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Allow Triton scans over non-last dimensions.

A Triton scan fusion processes the whole scan dimension inside each block, so its output tile sizes have no entry for that dimension. `TritonFusion::GetLaunchConfig` matched the tile sizes with the leading dimensions of the fusion root, which gives the right number of blocks only when the scan dimension is last. `CanTritonHandleScan` therefore rejected all other scans.

Skip the scan dimensions when counting tiles, and remove the check from `CanTritonHandleScan`. The scan dimensions are found by walking from the fusion roots through get-tuple-element and elementwise ops, as `TilingSpace` does.

`ScanRewriterTriton` still only rewrites scans over the minor-most dimension of the layout, so only scans over a dimension that is minor-most but not last are newly rewritten.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026270874

[XLA:GPU] Allow reverse scans in Triton.

The Triton scan emitter already handles reverse scans: it visits the tiles in reverse order and takes the carry from the first element of each tile. Padding a partial tile with zeros stays correct because only additive combiners are supported.

Remove the check from `CanTritonHandleScan`, so that `ScanRewriterTriton` also rewrites reverse scans.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Avoid hoisting parallel or oversized while loops

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Avoid hoisting parallel or oversized while loops

`SmallWhileLoopHoistingPass` runs after `ParallelTaskAssigner` and hoists any
loop below a 1 GB accessed byte limit without checking for multi threaded
operations or body kernel count. `ThunkSequenceKernelEmitter` lowers hoisted
loops to a single workgroup kernel, which serializes partitioned fusions,
multi workgroup dot kernels, and large copies onto one thread. Linking hundreds
of array loop kernels into one LLVM module also causes severe compile time
regressions.

Exclude instructions with `outer_dimension_partitions` above 1, codegen `kDot`
and `kOutput` dot fusions that emit multiple workgroups, and parallel or layout
changing `kCopy` instructions, sharing workgroup and copy predicates with
`DotOpEmitter` and `CopyThunk`. Lower the default
`xla_cpu_small_while_loop_byte_threshold` to 2 MiB and cap hoisted body kernel
and instruction counts while preserving scalar slice update loops and explicit
`xla_cpu_small_call` multi workgroup lowering.

Fixes openxla/xla#53475 and openxla/xla#52122.

Tests:
- `//xla/backends/cpu/transforms:small_while_loop_hoisting_pass_test` pins
  partitioned fusions, scatter loops, parallel dots, copies, and body caps.
- `//xla/service/cpu/tests:cpu_while_test` exercises end to end hoisting
  exclusions and explicit `xla_cpu_small_call` multi workgroup execution.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Recalibrate ParallelTaskAssigner cost model and skip scatter fusions

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Recalibrate ParallelTaskAssigner cost model and skip scatter fusions

`DefaultCostModel` counts scalar ops without accounting for target SIMD width,
underweights transcendental and scalar libm calls, and drops by 26x to 10 KiB
per thread once the flop to byte ratio passes 1.0. Small integer and polynomial
fusions pay thread pool overhead while medium transcendental fusions stay capped
at low thread counts. `ParallelTaskAssigner` also sets
`outer_dimension_partitions` on scatter fusions even though `CpuScatterFusion`
emits one workgroup.

Replace that heuristic with a roofline execution time model over target vector
width, enabled subtarget features, vectorized intrinsic and scalar libm costs,
reduction and transpose structure, and tiered memory bandwidth with dispatch
overhead. Cache probed subtarget vector width and enabled features on
`TargetMachineFeatures` to keep compile time unchanged. Skip single threaded
scatter fusions so partition metadata reflects actual parallel execution.

Part of openxla/xla#53475.

Tests:
- `//xla/service/cpu:parallel_task_assignment_test` pins scatter skipping, small
  bitwise and polynomial fusions, vector width scaling, vectorized and libm
  transcendentals, transposes, reductions, concatenates, and memory bound caps.
- `//xla/backends/cpu/codegen:target_machine_features_test` covers subtarget
  feature and vector register width queries.
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1027442131

head_commit.message:
Assign default 6-bit BitPlaneProto split layouts for FP6 and bump ABI.

6-bit floating-point formats (`F6E3M2FN` and `F6E2M3FN`) previously defaulted to 8-bit `(4, 1)` container tiling in device memory, wasting 25% of storage.

Assign `{1,0:T(16,128)BP(4:(8,1))(2:(16,1))}` (compact), `{1,0:T(T_0,128)(16,128)BP(4:(8,1))(2:(16,1))}` (large 2nd minor and `kMatchDimension`), and 1D `{0:T(2048)BP(4:(128)(8,1))(2:(128)(16,1))}` by default on TPU v5+ while preserving explicit `T(T_0, 128)(4, 1)` `fp6-in-8b` layouts across XLA:TPU HLO transforms and PJRT. Teach `TransferSizeUtil`, `Target`, `LiteralLinearizer`, and `CopyEmitter` to size, linearize, and DMA-transfer 3-sublane `(16, 128)` FP6 strips, and increment `kAbiCurrentMajorVersion`.

head_commit.message:
Add BitPlaneProto layout representation and rejection guards.

6-bit floating-point TPU layouts split each `(16, 128)` strip across non-adjacent 4-bit and 2-bit sublanes, whereas `LayoutProto.element_size_in_bits` (`E(n)`) specifies contiguous `n`-bit elements. Overloading `E(6)` broke contiguous `E(n)` semantics and layout size queries.

Add `BitPlaneProto` (`bit_planes` in `LayoutProto`, printed as `BP(w[:tiles])` or `BP(w@offset[:tiles])`) supporting both per-strip splits with outer `tiles` (such as `{1,0:T(256,128)(16,128)BP(4:(8,1))(2:(16,1))}` and `{0:T(2048)BP(4:(128)(8,1))(2:(128)(16,1))}`) and whole-tensor splits with empty outer `tiles` (such as 64-bit integer `{1,0:BP(32:(8,128))(32:(8,128))}`), while keeping `sizeof(xla::Layout)` unchanged. Update `LayoutUtil`, `ShapeUtil`, `HloParser`, and Python `xc.Layout`, and guard unsupported CPU/GPU, generic PJRT, `TiledLinearizer`, and C API paths.

display_title: Add 6-bit BitPlaneProto strip linearization in TiledLinearizer.

head_commit.message:
Add 6-bit BitPlaneProto strip linearization in TiledLinearizer.

`TiledLinearizer` previously rejected all `BitPlaneProto` layouts with `UnimplementedError`, blocking host-to-device linearization and device-to-host delinearization for 6-bit floating-point TPU tensors.

Support 128-lane 6-bit `BP(4:...)(2:...)` split strip layouts (`{1,0:T(T_0,128)(16,128)BP(4:(8,1))(2:(16,1))}`, `{1,0:T(16,128)BP(4:(8,1))(2:(16,1))}`, and 0D/1D `{...T(2048)BP(4:(128)(8,1))(2:(128)(16,1))}`) in `TiledLinearizer` using Highway SIMD strip repack helpers (`Repack6BitStripToHardwareLayoutHighway` and `Repack6BitStripToHostLayoutHighway`) that pack 1-byte host strips into 3-sublane interleaved 4-bit/2-bit hardware strips and unpack them back to host layout, with checked 64-bit tile and strip size arithmetic.

Verified 0D/1D/2D/3D 6-bit `BP(...)` `TiledLinearizer` round-trips, unaligned 1D host buffers, dynamic metadata prefixes, non-contiguous host strides, partial strips, `set_padding_to_nan`, and element-type/layout/strip-size/overflow validation in unit tests.

head_commit.message:
Add BitPlaneProto layout representation.

6-bit floating-point TPU layouts split each `(16, 128)` strip across non-adjacent 4-bit and 2-bit sublanes, whereas `LayoutProto.element_size_in_bits` (`E(n)`) specifies contiguous `n`-bit elements. Overloading `E(6)` broke contiguous `E(n)` semantics and layout size queries.

Update `LayoutUtil`, `ShapeUtil`, `HloParser`, `LayoutAssignment`, HLO simplifiers, and Python `xc.Layout`, and guard unsupported CPU/GPU, generic PJRT, `TiledLinearizer`, and C API paths.

Verified `BitPlaneProto` parsing, contiguous bit-plane validation, `LogicalBitWidth`, `ShapeUtil` and HLO pass preservation and guards, `CommonPjRtClient::CopyToMemorySpace`, `_hlo.pyi` stubgen, and Python `xc.Layout` round-trips in unit tests.

Assign default 6-bit BitPlaneProto split layouts for FP6 and bump ABI.

Teach TPU transfer-size, target layout, literal linearizer, and copy lowering utilities to size, linearize, and DMA-transfer 3-sublane `(16, 128)` FP6 strips, and increment the TPU runtime ABI major version.

Verified ABI version checks, default `BP(...)` vs. `fp6-in-8b` and rank-0 scalar tiling, canonical memory-space layout validation, bit-plane reshape/slice bitcast checks, HLO layout/tiling passes, and literal linearizer round-trips in unit tests.

display_title: Add `PjRtClient::WatchExternalDmaRegions()` to subscribe to device memory regions exported as Linux dma-bufs for a given `PjRtMemorySpace`.

head_commit.message:
Add `PjRtClient::WatchExternalDmaRegions()` to subscribe to device memory regions exported as Linux dma-bufs for a given `PjRtMemorySpace`.

External DMA transports (such as RDMA memory registration) need to register exported dma-buf regions and unregister them before their file descriptors are closed. This change adds a `DmaBuf`-lifetime-driven watcher API on `PjRtClient` and implements it for StreamExecutor GPU clients via `GpuDmaBufCache`:
- Replays `on_register` for all currently live dma-buf regions on the memory space and notifies for any new cached or uncached dma-buf exports before returning from `AcquireExternalDmaAccess()`.
- Invokes `on_unregister` before closing a dma-buf fd (or when the watcher handle is destroyed) outside cache locks.
